This interesting project, created by Jeff Halter (introduced via Daring Fireball), lets users run original 68k After Dark screensaver modules on modern Macs. Details below.

"Running Classic After Dark Screensavers on Modern macOS"

Depending on when you started using or were exposed to Macs, you may remember After Dark—a collection of screensavers that were practically a staple on Macintosh computers in the 1990s. At the very least, you've probably heard of its famous Flying Toasters screensaver.

For years, running these classic screensavers typically required old hardware or a Classic Mac OS emulator, making setup rather cumbersome. However, a new project called Afterglow makes it considerably easier on modern Macs.

As John Gruber noted on Daring Fireball, the project was created by Jeff Halter, who previously developed Lunacy—a natively Swift-written application that lets users play the classic game Lunatic Fringe from More After Dark on modern Macs.

Afterglow runs original modules via an emulator specifically designed for After Dark modules, without requiring a full Classic Mac OS environment. Notably, Afterglow also includes a screensaver module for modern macOS, allowing users to set any imported After Dark module as their Mac's screensaver.

Here's Halter explaining the creative philosophy behind the project:

In the 1990s, Berkeley Systems' After Dark screensavers brought Flying Toasters, Fish, and Starry Skylines to every Macintosh screen. Beyond their practical function of preventing burn-in on CRT displays, they provided entertainment—their animations could be hilarious, surreal, beautiful, and sometimes nauseating. They are works of art worth preserving. Running After Dark modules today often requires complex Mac OS emulator setups or vintage hardware. Even then, no single emulator or old computer can run all modules perfectly: some animations run too fast, others too slow. Afterglow is an emulator designed specifically to run After Dark modules—it executes the original 68k module code, not a remake or port—and does not depend on ROMs or Classic Mac OS at all. In the spirit of software preservation, this project lets everyone easily enjoy After Dark today and for many years to come.

The project's website notes that Afterglow does not include After Dark module files, but provides tutorials for finding and importing modules into Afterglow.

Halter also mentioned that Afterglow includes built-in features such as module control, full-screen mode, random playback, multi-module support, 3D box art images, CRT rendering effects, resource viewer, and the DrawMorph editor.
